sentences.text: Coram:

Dr. Justice B.R. Sarangi
 Mr. Justice M.S.Raman
 Order
This matter is taken up through hybrid mode.

2. Heard Mr. S. Das, learned Senior Advocate along with Mr. H. Mohanty, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. S.N. Nayak learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State.
3.

The petitioner has filed this writ petition seeking direction to the opposite parties to pay the compensation to the petitioner from the date of forcible dispossession of his land and such other benefits as is available under RFCTLA R&R Act, 2013.

4. Mr. S. Das, learned Senior Advocate appearing for the petitioner contended that since the petitioner has been forcible dispossessed, he is entitled to get the compensation and also other benefits as is available under 2013 Act.

5. A counter affidavit has been filed by opposite party no.1, wherein at paragraphs-8 and 14 it has been stated as follows:-
8.

That in reply to the averments made in Para-3 of the writ petition it is humbly submitted that the Notification U/s 3(A) was published vide S.O No. 2021 (E) dtd.
01.07.2015 and published in the Extra Ordinary Central Gazette part-II U/s 3(A)(2)
vide No. 1545 dtd. 23.07.2015 which was the cut off date for this project for fixation of Market Value etc.
The above ARUN Digitally signed by Notification was also published in two local daily newspapers ARUN KUMAR KUMAR MISHRA for wide publication among the land owners.

As such the Date: 2023.05.12 MISHRA 18:04:01 +05'30' petitioner has got ample opportunity to make objection if any within the Kintalu Chandra Sekhar Patro @ vs The Land Acquisition Officer And ..... ... on 12 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49377144/
1 period of 21 days from the date of 3(A) (3) Notification of the NH Act.

entities.text: Kintalu Chandra Sekhar Patro @ vs The Land Acquisition Officer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But no such objection is made by him within the stipulated period on this particular plot.
The period of objection was elapsed on 09.11.2015.
Hence the plea taken by the petitioner on forcibly taking over possession of his land by Opp. Party is quite misleading.

14. That in reply to the averments made in Para-10 of the writ petition it is humbly submitted that the petitioner was paid compensation amount with regards to the others plots covered under Acquisition, which was already Notified for this project on 23.07.2018 through RTGS mode.

Payment of compensation for the left out Plot No.
1093/2206 will also be paid after completion of all statutory formalities under NH Act -1956.
6. In view of the aforesaid fact and circumstances since the land of the petitioner has not been acquired, the benefit as claimed by the petitioner may not be admissible.
However it is contended by Mr. S. Das, learned Senior Advocate that in the subsequent notification, the land of the petitioner has been acquired.
7. If that be so, it is open to the petitioner to approach the appropriate authority for grant of compensation and other benefits as due and admissible to him in accordance with law.
8. With that observation the writ petition stands disposed of.

(DR. B.R. SARANGI)
 JUDGE Arun (M.S. RAMAN)
